rules.name: ^php(56|70|71|72|73|74|80|81|82|83|84)-php(-[a-z0-9_-]+)?$
rules.fix:
yum -y install https://extras.getpagespeed.com/release-latest.rpm
yum upgrade '{scl}-php*'
systemctl restart {scl}-php-fpm

rules.name: ^php(-[a-z0-9_-]+)?$
rules.fix:
yum -y install https://extras.getpagespeed.com/release-latest.rpm
yum --enablerepo=getpagespeed-extras-php{nodot} upgrade 'php-*'
systemctl restart php-fpm

rules.name: ^(php(56|70|71|72|73|74|80|81|82|83)-)?php(-[a-z0-9_-]+)?$
rules.note: Remi stopped building for CentOS 7 in June 2024, so every Remi EL7 build predates the fix.
rules.fix:
# No patched Remi build exists for CentOS 7. Move to the GetPageSpeed PHP 8.4 stack:
yum -y install https://extras.getpagespeed.com/release-latest.rpm
yum-config-manager --enable getpagespeed-extras-php84
yum install php84-getpagespeed-stack

rules.name: ^php(-[a-z0-9_-]+)?$
rules.note: CentOS 7 is end-of-life and its PHP 5.4 package will never get this fix.
rules.fix:
# CentOS 7 PHP 5.4 will never be fixed. Move to the GetPageSpeed PHP 8.4 stack:
yum -y install https://extras.getpagespeed.com/release-latest.rpm
yum-config-manager --enable getpagespeed-extras-php84
yum install php84-getpagespeed-stack

rules.name: ^php(-[a-z0-9_-]+)?$
rules.note: On October 23, 2026 Red Hat still listed the php:8.4 stream on RHEL 9 as affected with no fix available. Switch to the fixed php:8.3 stream or watch dnf updateinfo list --cve CVE-2026-109618.

sudo systemctl restart php-fpm httpd

rules.name: ^php(8\.\d)?(-[a-z0-9_-]+)?$
rules.eol_note: Red Hat's advisories cover only some streams of this branch. Ask dnf directly: dnf updateinfo list --cve CVE-2026-109618
rules.fix:
sudo dnf upgrade 'php*'
sudo systemctl restart php-fpm httpd

rules.name: ^php8\.\d(-[a-z0-9_-]+)?$
rules.eol_note: Amazon Linux 2023 fixed php8.2 to php8.5 only.
rules.fix:
sudo dnf upgrade --releasever=latest 'php*'
sudo systemctl restart php-fpm httpd

rules.name: ^(php\d(\.\d)?|libapache2-mod-php\d(\.\d)?)(-[a-z0-9_-]+)?$
rules.note: Ubuntu backports the fix and keeps the original PHP version number.
rules.fix:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install --only-upgrade $(dpkg -l 'php*' | awk '/^ii/{print $2}')
sudo systemctl restart 'php*-fpm.service' apache2
